uplink.description: Status report: gang0 vibrating, gang1 idle, battery 3.0 V (TTN example bytes; report type 0x01)
uplink._note: Upstream example status-report input. Upstream oracle: Volt 3, status1 = bytes[4] = 1 -> gang0 vibrating, status2 = bytes[5] = 0 -> gang1 idle. expected.data authored to the normalized vocabulary (one channels[] entry per gang, each with its own action.motion.detected), not copied from upstream's Volt/status1/status2 output. The positions DIFFER here, so the two entries cannot be transposed unnoticed - the case the old top-level either-gang OR could not express. `motion` resolves through the entries; action.motion.count is the whole-device roll-up and stays top-level.

uplink.description: Status report: gang0 idle, gang1 vibrating, battery 3.6 V
uplink._note: Synthetic in-bounds frame. byte3=36 -> 3.6 V; byte4=0 -> gang0 idle; byte5=1 -> gang1 vibrating. The inverse per-position states from vector 1 at the same count of 1, so a swapped-entry bug shows up in exactly one of the two vectors.

uplink.description: Status report: both gangs vibrating, low battery flag set (2.8 V)
uplink._note: byte[3]=0x9C -> high bit set (lowBattery), low 7 bits 0x1C=28 -> 2.8 V; status1=status2=1 -> both gangs vibrating, roll-up count 2. battery/lowBattery are whole-device readings and stay top-level, outside the channels[] entries.

uplink.description: Status report: no vibration on either gang
uplink._note: Both status bytes zero -> neither gang detecting, roll-up count 0; still a valid measurement frame, and both entries are still emitted (no disconnected-gang sentinel exists in this format).
